title: A dev checkout reports a version distinguishable from the last published one, derived at build time
description:
Filed by orchestrator ruling, 2026-09-15, when QCLI-271 AC5 was DECLINED for 0.7.0. AC5 asked that the question be decided and recorded -- either implemented or declined with the reason -- so declining with the reason recorded satisfies it as written. This task carries the implementation, deliberately scoped POST-0.7.0.

The problem AC5 named is real and cost a release: QCLI-271 exists because QCLI-266s fix sat on dev, unreleased, while `quest --version` reported the same string for a dev checkout carrying the fix and for the published package that did not. Nothing a caller could run distinguished them.

THE REASON FOR DECLINING, recorded so it is not relitigated: the version string already has EIGHT hand-maintained copies -- root package.json, the six npm/quest-<platform>/package.json manifests, and .claude-plugin/plugin.json (itself found stale at 0.6.0 through two releases during the 0.7.0 bump). A dev-distinguishable version that is another hand-edited value adds a ninth site to drift, making the disease worse than the symptom.

THE ONLY SHAPE THAT DOES NOT ADD A DRIFT SITE is a build-time suffix DERIVED rather than typed -- git describe (or equivalent) inside the packaging pipeline, so a dev checkout reports something like 0.7.0-dev.<n>.g<sha> while a published build reports the bare version, with no human maintaining the difference. That is a change to scripts/build-platform-packages.mjs and the version surface, which is mid-release and not the place to change now.

Constraint for whoever implements it: whatever is derived must NOT become a seventh/eighth thing a release has to remember to bump. If the implementation adds a hand-edited site, it has failed its own purpose. See docs/runbooks/quest-cli-package-and-release.md, "What a version bump touches".

acceptanceCriteria.text: A checkout with commits beyond the last release tag reports a version distinguishable from the published one, verified by running the built binary from such a checkout rather than by reading the code
A build from a release tag reports the bare release version, unchanged from todays behaviour, verified the same way

The distinguishing part is DERIVED at build time (git describe or equivalent), adding zero new hand-edited version sites -- confirmed against the version-bump file list in docs/runbooks/quest-cli-package-and-release.md
The release runbooks version-bump section states whether this changed what a bump touches

plan: Files: scripts/build-platform-packages.mjs (derive + inject); src/application/version.ts (version surface); a new test for the derivation; docs/runbooks/quest-cli-package-and-release.md; .quest/ (this record).

Derivation (in scripts/build-platform-packages.mjs): run git describe --tags --long on the checkout. If it fails, or if git describe --tags --exact-match HEAD succeeds, the derived version is the bare root package.json version. Otherwise parse vX.Y.Z-N-gSHA into X.Y.Z-dev.N.gSHA (strip the leading v; replace -N-g with -dev.N.g). The base stays root package.json / src/application/version.ts, so no new hand-edited site is added.

Injection: extend the existing bun build --compile step with --define __QUEST_BUILD_VERSION__ set to the derived string as a quoted literal, so the compiled binary embeds the derived value and a release-tag build embeds the bare value.

Version surface: src/application/version.ts declares the injected global for typecheck and reports it when it is a string (typeof guard), else the existing literal. Under bun test and bun run src/cli/main.ts the global is undefined, so in-process tests and dev runtime keep reporting the bare version.

AC1 acceptance: on this branch (57 commits past v0.12.0) run QUEST_BUN_TARGET=darwin-arm64 bun run build:packages, then ./npm/quest-darwin-arm64/bin/quest --version; expect 0.12.0-dev.57.ga45f84f7 and assert it differs from 0.12.0 -- verified by running the built binary, not by reading code.
AC2 acceptance: git worktree add at tag v0.12.0, build the native binary there, run ./npm/quest-darwin-arm64/bin/quest --version; expect exactly 0.12.0, bare and unchanged.

AC3 acceptance: diff the changed files against the hand-edited site list in docs/runbooks/quest-cli-package-and-release.md section What a version bump touches; show no new typed site was added (the suffix exists only at build time in scripts/build-platform-packages.mjs).
AC4 acceptance: docs/runbooks/quest-cli-package-and-release.md What a version bump touches updated to state the dev suffix is build-derived and the bump-touches list is unchanged.
Regression guard: keep test/contract/cli-process.test.ts:30 and test/cli-tracker-process.test.ts:125 green (in-process --version still equals source QUEST_VERSION).

Overlap: opum-ai/quest-cli#486 (parked; branch chore/QCLI-433-bump-0-13-0) also edits src/application/version.ts and package.json; the only overlapping file is src/application/version.ts. Reported, not resolved -- do not touch #486 or its branch.
implementationNotes:
Second independent report, 2026-09-15, from opum-fleet -- unprompted and from outside this repository, which is what makes it worth recording here rather than only in a reply.

What it measured (its numbers, re-verified here before writing this note): the installed 0.7.1 returns top-level keys schemaVersion, contractVersion, kind, data, principal for "quest task list --status In Progress --json" -- no "scope". This checkouts dev carries QCLI-316, which adds it, and git show dev:package.json still reads 0.7.1. npm confirms 0.7.1 is published and is dist-tag latest. So the published bytes and the dev bytes genuinely differ and "quest --version" reports the same string for both: exactly the failure mode this task was filed to end, now observed by a consumer rather than by this repository.

The consequence it reported is the one that matters for priority. opum-sdlc cannot gate on the version, so it now tells sessions to detect "scope" by KEY PRESENCE and fall through when absent. That works and needs nothing from us -- but it is a consumer writing a workaround around a defect we have filed and not fixed, which is the cost this task is measuring. opum-fleet also hit the same shape against its own held plugin version (OFLE-71) and has written it up as a fleet pattern rather than a single-tool quirk, so quest-cli is now one of at least two instances.

Nothing in the declined-shape reasoning above changes: the fix must still be DERIVED at build time and must still add zero hand-edited version sites.

Dependency exchange, Phase A. lore-web (origin/dev at 281e431) confirms it consumes quest only via the exact-equality version guard ci.yml:149 (fail-closed), the .data.length of quest task list --json, and the exit code of quest agents --check; it installs only the published npm artifact and never a dev checkout, so a dev version suffix never reaches those paths (git grep for semver / satisfies / sort -V: no matches). QCLI-296 does not break lore-web. Verified their boundary caveat: src/application/agents/agent-instructions.ts lines 163-181 compares by string substitution, not semver, so agents --check reports version-only (exit 0) on a dev-suffixed version -- no false drift. Behavior note, not a blocker: running --update-instructions from a dev build would write the suffixed string into CLAUDE.md, whereas a release-tag build writes the bare version, which is what the runbook prescribes.

Checkpoint for DEC-158 (36) renewal, 2026-10-04T20:37Z. Phase A complete and accepted: task started, plan recorded (10 items), lore-web dependency answered, and the opum-ai/quest-cli#486 overlap measured at exactly one file (src/application/version.ts). Branch feat/QCLI-296-derived-dev-version, two tracker-only commits, no code changes yet, no PR. Working tree clean. Next step: Phase B implementation (after opum-workflow 0.13.4) -- derive a dev version suffix at build time in scripts/build-platform-packages.mjs via git describe, inject it into the compiled binary with bun build --compile --define, and make src/application/version.ts prefer the injected value with a bare-version fallback; then update docs/runbooks/quest-cli-package-and-release.md and run the per-criterion acceptance commands.

Phase B (DEC-158 (40), attempt quest-cli-r40-2). Implemented and committed f7c60554 on feat/QCLI-296-derived-dev-version (6 files: scripts/derive-build-version.ts new; scripts/build-platform-packages.mjs; src/application/version.ts; test/qcli296-derived-dev-version.test.ts new; test/contract/tracker/lore-adapter-boundary.test.ts; docs/runbooks/quest-cli-package-and-release.md). Tree clean, not pushed, no PR. Checks green under the pinned bun 1.4.2 (typecheck, lint, format, layer, new unit test, three version suites). AC1 mechanism proven by compiled binary: with the injected define the binary reports 0.12.0-dev.61.gf7c60554, without it and in-process it reports bare 0.12.0. BLOCKER: the accepted plan distinguishes a release build from a dev build by git describe --tags --exact-match, which never matches at release-build time -- the release bytes are built by the qualification workflow against the untagged branch and the tag is created later (prepublication-qualification.yml:140-141; runbook step 2 vs step 5; release.yml:34-37). So a release build would embed a dev suffix, and prepublish.mjs (run at prepublication-qualification.yml:147) throws candidate-version-is-not-semver at :258, blocking every future release; AC2 is unreachable as written. Escalated to team-lead for a design decision (recommendation: gate the suffix on an explicit release signal that only the pipeline sets). PR held pending that decision.
